before noun: › [ before noun ] specialized geology relating to or caused by an earthquake

NONE: › having very great and damaging effects

example: The news that the chairman would resign set off seismic waves in the business community.
主席要辭職的消息在商界引發了劇烈震撼。

NONE: › a piece of equipment that measures and records the strength of an earthquake
› the scientific study of the sudden, violent movements of the earth connected with earthquakes

T: B2 [ T ] to take something quickly and keep or hold it
C2 [ T ] to take using sudden force
› [ T ] If the police or other officials seize something, they take possession of it with legal authority.

usually passive: › [ usually passive ] If a strong emotion or pain seizes you, you feel it suddenly.

example: I seized his arm and made him turn to look at me.
我抓住他的手臂，使他轉身看著我。
He seized the chance/opportunity of a free flight with both hands (= with eagerness or enthusiasm).
他急切地緊抓住搭乘免費航班的機會。
The rebels have seized ten soldiers to use as hostages.
叛亂者俘獲了十名士兵作爲人質。
Political instability helped the army to seize power.
政治動盪使軍隊攫取了權力。
Troops yesterday seized control of the broadcasting station.
昨天部隊奪取了廣播電台的控制權。
Customs officers at Heathrow have seized 60 kilos of heroin.
希思洛機場的海關官員查獲了60公斤海洛因。
I was suddenly seized by/with a feeling of great insecurity and loneliness.
我突然感到很沒有安全感，很孤獨。

NONE: › to use, accept, or take advantage of something quickly or enthusiastically

example: The story was seized on by the tabloid press, who printed it under huge headlines.
那件事被小報緊抓著不放，並用巨大標題刊載。

NONE: › to stop being able to move or work in the normal way

example: The washing machine totally seized up on Thursday.
星期四的時候洗衣機徹底壞掉了。
The traffic had seized up for miles because of the roadworks.
由於道路施工，車輛堵了好幾英里。

C or U: › [ C or U ] the action of taking something by force or with legal authority
佔領，奪取，攫取；查封，沒收，充公

C: › [ C ] a very sudden attack of an illness in which someone becomes unconscious or develops violent movements
› [ C ] old use a sudden failure of the heart

example: Seizures of illicit drugs have increased by 30 percent this year.
今年，查獲的違禁藥品增加了30%。
an epileptic seizure
癲癇突發
His aunt died of a seizure.
他的姑姑死於心臟病突發。
figurative humorous When I told her how much it cost she nearly had a seizure (= she was very shocked).
我告訴她花了多少錢時，她差一點嚇出病來。
